Untiled, the original Qwen-Image-2.1 pricing: 4000 bytes per pixel per element byte plus 0.6 GiB, rounded up to a whole MiB, with the bf16 decode raised to cover its 1024px point by the shipped margin; the encode is priced as the decode (the encoder is narrower, 96 vs 144 base channels, so this is an upper bound), and decode_large_bf16, which only MIOpen prices on, as decode_bf16. A tiled stand-in's slope is two RGBA copies of the image per pixel (16 bytes in bf16, 32 in fp32); the base of the bf16 decode covers the 768px tile by the shipped margin, the other lines take it scaled by the element size, unmeasured.
No Qwen-Image-2.1 point is measured under cudaMallocAsync: priced with the native allocator's stand-ins, the larger of the two on cuDNN (cudaMallocAsync needs 25-35% less).

Fitted lines are working_memory/fit.py's: the upper envelope of the in-fit points of this entry's lines, plus 5%; a tiled line covers what its points measured above the untiled demand at their tile, per pixel of the tile, as MIOpen's tiled cost grows mostly with the tile rather than the frame (qwen_image_2_1/vae.py, `_line`).
